spm_overworld_sprites:
Sprite map of the world map scene $FE: 14 animations, 48 sprite-groups. scene_meta_00FE loads it ($1238 bytes) with gfx_overworld_actors and pal_overworld_sprites (colour $90; music bgm_beautiful_world). The animation index is a word of the party array ($0D60-$0D6A) that WorldMapController writes to actor field $28 of the leader and companion dots.

=== ANIMATIONS ===

Box = extent box in px, parts per frame. Holds are in ticks - 1 (hold 7 = 8 ticks).
- #00 sprite_set_00001C: 4 distinct frames, hold 7, 23-31 x 43-46 px, 6-7 parts (the largest of the walkers).
- #01 sprite_set_00002E: frames A B A C, hold 7, 20-21 x 32-33 px, 7-10 parts.
- #02 sprite_set_000040, #03 sprite_set_000052, #04 sprite_set_000064: frames A B A C, hold 7, 15-16 x 32-33 px, 5-8 parts.
- #05 sprite_set_000076: frames A B A C, hold 7, 15-16 x 40-41 px, 7-10 parts.
- #06 sprite_set_000088: frames A B A C, hold 7, one 16 x 16 part (tile words $083A, $085A, $083A, $485A: the last frame H-flipped).
- #07 sprite_set_00009A, #08 sprite_set_0000B0, #09 sprite_set_0000C6, #0A sprite_set_0000DC: 5 frames A B C D C, holds 7, 7, 7, 9, 7, 32 px wide, 48-75 px tall, 11-13 parts. WorldMapController's wa79_neil fills the party array with 7, 8, 9, A for the Watermia to Euro leg, so these four look like the pieces of one vehicle (not checked at runtime, OQ-B001-2).
- #0B sprite_set_0000F2: 3 frames, hold 1, box 79 x 48 px, 24 parts; the leader of the Dao to Over Babel trip (daC8_neil).
- #0C sprite_set_000100: 3 frames, hold 1, box 79 x 48 px, 27 parts; no writer found.
- #0D sprite_set_00010E: 4 frames, hold 9, 48-64 x 64 px, 14-22 parts; the leader of the Watermia to South Cape trip (wa78_men).

Which art animations #00 to #05 draw (which party member) was not checked.

=== FORMAT ===

A sprite map file has three layers (same format as the spriteset_* files, see spriteset_freedan):
- Pointer table (the first label): one word per animation index. The engine reads entry $28 of the actor (UpdateActorAnimation: table + 2 x $28), then the frame record $2A x 4 inside that list.
- Sprite-set (frame list): 4-byte records < hold, &sprite_group >, closed by a hidden $FFFF. A frame is shown for hold + 1 ticks.
- Sprite-group: 12 header bytes, the part count, then 7-byte sprite-parts. Bytes 0-3 are the X extents (left, right) and Y extents (above, below) of the frame box; UpdateActorAnimation loads them into $18/$1C and $1A/$1E and swaps each pair for a flipped actor. Bytes 4-7 are a tile-unit box (X offset, Y offset, width and height in 16-pixel units) read by PlayerAttackHitTest and the solid-rectangle COP handlers; bytes 8-11 are the body box (X offset, width, Y offset, height in pixels, signed offsets) read by CombatCollision and the interaction collision code.
- Sprite-part < size, x, x', y, y', tile word >: size 0 = 8 x 8, 1 = 16 x 16 (the OAM size bit); x and y are offsets inside the extent box, x' and y' the offsets used when the actor is H / V flipped (x + x' = box width - part width); the tile word is an OAM word (bit 8 name table, bits 9-11 palette, bits 12-13 priority, $4000 H flip, $8000 V flip) that the engine XORs with the actor's attribute word $0E.
Every group of this file carries the engine's default boxes ($F8 $F0 $01 $01 and $F8 $10 $F0 $10): the same eight bytes are in all 85 groups of spm_boot_logos, spm_title_actors, spm_darkspace_sprites and spm_overworld_sprites.
spriteset_adrift_wave:
Spriteset of the adrift-sequence wave effect (Bank 14, 14C0CA-14C12B): one animation of four single-sprite frames. Its only user is gold_ship/adrift/dc2F_adrift_fx, one of the four tile-streaming effect actors (cop_handlers_sprite): it sets the art source with SetScratchPointer ( misc_fx_1CD180 ), passes spriteset_adrift_wave to SetMetasprite, starts animation 0 with SetTileStreamAnim ( #00, #$2010 ) and loops AdvanceSpriteAnim. Each AdvanceSpriteAnim stages one frame of art from the source to VRAM word $2010 (the NMI does the DMA) and takes the hold time from this table. That file's header describes the result as ocean waves over the adrift scene. The old header called it a set of non-combat environmental particles.

Structure (same as every spriteset): spriteset_adrift_wave is the animation-index table (one word pointer here); sprite_set_adrift_wave_loop is that animation's frame list of 4-byte records < hold word, &sprite-group > ended by a hidden $FFFF; each sprite-group is a 13-byte header followed by one 7-byte sprite-part. All four frames hold $0007 (8 ticks each, 32 ticks per loop) and have identical headers. The last word of the sprite-part ($0A00, $0A04, $0A08, $0A0C) is the only difference: for a tile-streaming animation its low byte is the art offset in 32-byte tiles (AdvanceSpriteAnim copies from animScratch + 32 x byte at +$12 of the frame data), and because the sprite-part's first byte is nonzero each frame is 128 bytes (four tiles), so the four frames are consecutive 128-byte pictures at offsets 0, 128, 256 and 384 of misc_fx_1CD180. The high byte $0A is not interpreted by the streaming code (open, OQ-I062-1).

Checked: file decoded against the sprite-set / sprite-group / sprite-part structs, the cop_handlers_sprite description of SetTileStreamAnim / AdvanceSpriteAnim, the only consumer read in full, and a whole-extraction search for spriteset_adrift_wave and sprite_set_adrift_wave_loop (no other reference). Not traced at runtime (UNVERIFIED-RUNTIME): what the frames look like and the exact bytes the DMA moves.
spriteset_freejia_tilefx:
Two Freejia tile animations (Bank 14, 1359872-1360072). It is a spriteset only in format: its one user streams the frames into VRAM as tiles, it holds no door or switch sprites (the old note was a guess from the name).

The only user is fr32_laborer_npc (Freejia): two actors run SetScratchPointer(misc_fx_1CD080) (the tile art), SetMetasprite(spriteset_freejia_tilefx), SetTileStreamAnim and AdvanceSpriteAnim. code_05B021 plays animation 0 into VRAM word $3FE0, code_05B03E (spawned by it) plays animation 1 into VRAM word $3FF0. The two destinations are one 4bpp tile apart ($10 words = 32 bytes).

=== WHAT AdvanceSpriteAnim READS ===

Only the size flag of the first sub-sprite (group +$0D, 0 = a 32-byte tile DMA here) and its tile byte (group +$12, times 32 = offset in the art). The other header and sub-sprite fields are not read on this path. General struct format: see spriteset_freedan.

=== CONTENT ===

- Animation 0: 4 frames, hold 7 (8 ticks, a 32-tick loop), groups 14C028-14C064, tile bytes 0, 1, 2, 3.
- Animation 1: 4 frames, hold 6 (7 ticks, a 28-tick loop), groups 14C078-14C0B4, tile bytes 4, 5, 6, 7 (tile words $0604-$0607; the high byte is not read here).
- All 8 groups are alike: header extents 8, 0, 8, 0, default boxes, one size-0 sub-sprite at offset 0, 0. Each frame is one 8x8 tile.

What the tiles show is not known: the actors have no movement code, although the file header of fr32_laborer_npc speaks of a walking laborer (OQ-I064-2).
spriteset_shadow:
Shadow player spriteset (Bank 14, 1343488-1355931 = $14:8000): every frame the player can show in form 2. 76 animations ($00-$4B), 261 frame records, 168 sprite groups, 1273 sub-sprites (at most 14 per group). Chosen by body_table rows $02 and $03 (spriteset bank $94, art shad_sprites_1BC000; row $03 is a copy, OQ-I061-1); SetActorBody copies the table pointer and bank into the actor ($7F0006, $7F0008). The animation numbering is shared with spriteset_will and spriteset_freedan, and the struct format (table, frame list, group header, sub-sprite) is described once, in the spriteset_freedan block note.

The old header ('walking, idle, attack and liquify animation frames', 'Shadow's unique morph poses') named poses the code does not use: 'liquify' appears nowhere outside the headers of this file and spriteset_shadow_fx, and the table has the same 76 indices as the Freedan table. Shadow's separate mode body is spriteset_shadow_aura_body (body_table row $08) and the effect sprites are in spriteset_shadow_fx.

=== WHAT DIFFERS FROM THE FREEDAN TABLE (same indices, other frame counts) ===

- Idle $00-$07 and $10-$17 are one frame with hold 9 (10 ticks). The player scripts stage $10-$13 for Shadow only; they use groups of their own (for example $00 shows sprite_group_148544, $10 shows sprite_group_14857B).
- Walk $08-$0F is 6 frames of hold 7 (Freedan 4 frames).
- Climb poses: the vine cycle $19-$1B, the ladder idles $2A-$2B and $2E-$2F and the detach poses $30-$31 and $34-$35 are one-frame lists (Freedan: 4 frames each); the ladder move $2C-$2D and the shimmy $32-$33 are 6 frames (holds 7, 3, 3, 7, 3, 3; Freedan 20 and 5); $18 is 4 frames (holds 9, 6, 4, 9). Other lists: $1C is 11 frames (holds 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 0), $1D-$25 are one frame each, $26-$29 are 4 frames.
- Melee attack $36-$39 is 7 frames (holds 3, 2, 1, 0, 0, 1, 2 = 16 ticks), the same frame count as Freedan; guard $3A-$3D is 8 frames of hold 0 (Freedan 4); $42-$43 and $48-$49 are 7 frames, $44-$47 and $4A-$4B one frame of hold 0.
- $3E-$41 (7 frames, holds 3, 1, 8, 4, 3, 3, 8) is not staged by the player scripts.

=== CHECKS ===

All 168 groups have a count byte equal to their number of sub-sprites, all 168 keep the default attack box $F8 $F0 $01 $01, all are referenced, all 76 frame lists are 4n + 2 bytes long (the label spacing of 75 consecutive lists was checked by hand) and 12443 bytes = 152 (table) + 4 x 261 + 2 x 76 (lists and their hidden $FFFF terminators) + 13 x 168 + 7 x 1273.
spriteset_snake_pit_fx:
Snake pit effect tile animation (Bank 14, 1360172-1360280). It is a spriteset only in format: its one user streams the frames into VRAM as tiles, it is not a library of particle sprites.

The only user is awB4_snake_pit_fx (Angkor Wat snake pit): SetScratchPointer(misc_fx_1CD380) names the tile art, SetMetasprite(spriteset_snake_pit_fx) names this table, SetTileStreamAnim(0, $2020) picks animation 0 and the VRAM word address $2020, and AdvanceSpriteAnim runs the frames.

=== WHAT AdvanceSpriteAnim READS ===

On this tile-streaming path only two bytes of each sprite group matter: the size flag of its first sub-sprite (group +$0D: 0 = 32 bytes, nonzero = 128 bytes = four 4bpp tiles) and the tile byte of that sub-sprite (group +$12, times 32 = the offset of the frame in the art). The extents, the two collision boxes and the X/Y offsets are not read here. The frame hold is the usual word (hold n lasts n + 1 ticks).

=== CONTENT ===

One animation (the table has one entry): 6 frame records, hold 5 (6 ticks each, a 36-tick loop), showing 4 distinct groups in the order 0, 1, 2, 3, 2, 1 (a ping-pong). Each group has the default header (extents 8, 8, 16, 0 and the boxes $F8 $F0 $01 $01 / $F8 $10 $F0 $10) and one sub-sprite of size 1 with tile word $0E00, $0E04, $0E08, $0E0C. Tile bytes 0, 4, 8, $0C are four 128-byte frames laid back to back in misc_fx_1CD380; each is DMAed to VRAM word $2020. The high byte $0E of the tile word (palette / priority bits in an OAM word) is not read by this path.

General format of the sprite-set / sprite-group / sprite-part structs: see the block note of spriteset_freedan.

The previous note ('sparkles, dust and other lightweight ambient particles') was a guess from the name: nothing but the snake pit effect uses this block.
